question: Which sequence lists the seven main taxonomic ranks in biological classification from the broadest (largest) group to the most specific group?
options: Kingdom → Phylum → Class → Order → Family → Genus → Species
Kingdom → Class → Phylum → Order → Family → Genus → Species
Phylum → Kingdom → Order → Class → Genus → Family → Species
Kingdom → Phylum → Order → Class → Family → Species → Genus

question: How is a biological species (物種) defined?
options: A group of organisms that live in the exact same habitat and eat the same food
A group of organisms with similar characteristics that can interbreed freely under natural conditions to produce fertile offspring
Any two organisms that belong to the same genus
A group of organisms that share the exact same coat colour

question: A mule (produced by crossing a male donkey and a female horse) is sterile (infertile), which demonstrates that donkeys and horses belong to different species.
In the binomial system of naming organisms (雙名法) introduced by Linnaeus, how is the scientific name of human beings written correctly?
options: Homo sapiens (italicized or underlined, with Genus capitalized and species lowercase)

question: Which characteristic distinguishes organisms in the Kingdom Prokaryotae (原核生物界 / Eubacteria and Archaea) from all other kingdoms?
options: They are all multicellular and heterotrophic.
Their cells lack a membrane-bound nucleus and membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria.
Their cell walls are always made of cellulose.
They carry out photosynthesis using chloroplasts.

question: In the six-kingdom classification system, prokaryotic organisms are divided into Kingdom Eubacteria (真細菌界) and Kingdom Archaebacteria (古細菌界) based on differences in cell wall composition, membrane lipids, and ribosomal RNA sequences.
Which kingdom consists mainly of unicellular eukaryotic organisms (such as Amoeba, Paramecium, and Euglena) as well as simple multicellular algae?
How do organisms in Kingdom Fungi (真菌界), such as mushrooms and bread mould, obtain their nutrition?
options: By photosynthesis using chlorophyll in their hyphae
By saprophytic or parasitic nutrition, secreting digestive enzymes onto external organic matter and absorbing the digested products
By ingesting solid food particles into a digestive tract
By chemosynthesis using inorganic sulphur compounds

question: Fungal cell walls are composed mainly of chitin (幾丁質) rather than cellulose, and fungi store excess carbohydrates as glycogen rather than starch.
Which group of plants lacks true roots, stems, leaves, and vascular tissues (xylem and phloem), and reproduces using spores produced inside capsules?
How do ferns (蕨類植物) differ from mosses?
options: Ferns produce flowers and seeds inside fruits.
Ferns possess true roots, stems, leaves, and vascular tissues (xylem and phloem), though they still reproduce by spores rather than seeds.
Ferns lack chlorophyll and are parasitic.
Ferns have no cuticle on their leaves.

question: Gymnosperms (裸子植物 / conifers) produce naked seeds inside cones (毬果) rather than enclosed inside fruits, and typically have needle-shaped leaves to reduce water loss.
Which combination of features is characteristic of dicotyledons (雙子葉植物) compared with monocotyledons (單子葉植物)?
options: One cotyledon, parallel leaf venation, and fibrous root system
Two cotyledons, net-like (reticulate) leaf venation, and a taproot system
One cotyledon, net-like leaf venation, and floral parts in multiples of four or five
Two cotyledons, parallel leaf venation, and scattered vascular bundles in the stem

question: Which phylum of invertebrates has jointed legs, a segmented body, and a hard chitinous exoskeleton (外骨骼)?
Earthworms belong to Phylum Annelida (環節動物門) and have soft, cylindrical bodies divided into many similar ring-like segments.
Which class of vertebrates has moist, scaleless skin used for gas exchange, lays jelly-coated eggs in water, and undergoes metamorphosis from aquatic larvae with gills to air-breathing adults?
Which two classes of vertebrates are homoiothermic (endothermic / 恆溫動物), maintaining a constant body temperature independent of the external environment?
options: Birds and Mammals / 鳥類和哺乳類

question: Reptiles (爬行類) have dry, scaly skin to prevent water loss and lay eggs with tough leathery shells on land, allowing them to live completely independent of water for reproduction.
Which feature is unique to Mammals (哺乳類) and absent in all other vertebrate classes?
options: Presence of a vertebral column and internal skeleton
Presence of hair/fur on the skin and mammary glands (乳腺) that produce milk to nourish young
Internal fertilization and lungs for breathing air

question: Why are viruses (病毒) NOT classified into any of the six kingdoms of living organisms?
options: They are too small to be seen under a light microscope.
They are non-cellular particles consisting only of a protein coat surrounding genetic material (DNA or RNA), and show no characteristics of life outside a host cell.
They cause infectious diseases in humans and plants.
They lack ribosomes and cell walls.

question: A dichotomous key (二叉式檢索表) identifies unknown organisms by presenting a series of paired, contrasting choices based on observable structural features.
Two organisms share the same Order and Family, while a third organism shares only the same Phylum and Class with them. Which two organisms are more closely related evolutionarily?
options: The two organisms in the same Family, because Family is a lower (more specific) taxonomic rank than Class
The organism in the same Phylum, because Phylum is a larger group
All three organisms are equally related
Evolutionary relatedness cannot be inferred from taxonomic ranks

question: Modern phylogenetic classification uses molecular evidence, such as comparing DNA base sequences and amino acid sequences of shared proteins, to determine evolutionary relationships more accurately.

[PLANT KINGDOM CLASSIFICATION] A biology student collects four plant specimens during a field trip: Specimen W has no vascular tissues and produces spores in capsules; Specimen X has vascular tissues and fronds with sori (spore-bearing structures) on the underside; Specimen Y produces cones with naked seeds; Specimen Z produces flowers and seeds enclosed in fruits. 1) Identify the major plant group to which each specimen (W, X, Y, and Z) belongs. 2) Explain why Specimens Y and Z are better adapted to dry terrestrial environments than Specimens W and X.
